Overview

Microsoft's transition to quantum-safe cryptography is a company-wide, multi-year change spanning encryption in transit, Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), and encryption at rest. Success requires more than publishing standards or building foundational components. Microsoft needs a reliable way to measure adoption, expose gaps, assign accountability, and drive decisions across organizations that own their own roadmaps. Key Management is a critical product area in the transition. Quantum-safe outcomes depend on the readiness of key-management services, key hierarchies, Hardware Security Modules (HSM) hardware and firmware, and related compliance dependencies.

As a Principal Product Manager for Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) Adoption & Key Management, you will define what readiness means, what Microsoft measures, and how leaders act on the evidence. You will work closely with the Key Management team on its PQC product strategy and roadmap, while using that product work as a proving ground for the broader adoption model. Your job is to make the transition concrete: clear requirements, measurable progress, explicit owners, sequenced dependencies, and credible commitments to leadership, customers, and regulators.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
 
 
In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day.


Responsibilities
  • Define PQC readiness and measurement. Own outcome targets, KPIs, scorecards, telemetry requirements, and adoption bars across encryption in transit, PKI, and encryption at rest.
  • Drive accountable cross-team results. Use existing governance and reviews to turn gaps or missed targets into named blockers, owners, decisions, and checkpoints.
  • Lead customer, field, compliance, and CELA engagement. Present Microsoft's PQC direction and translate customer, audit, regulatory, and government requirements into product priorities and timelines.
  • Own the product roadmap and adoption narrative. Publish clear PQC roadmaps and guidance that distinguish committed capabilities from plans, dependencies, exceptions, and open decisions.
  • Support Key Management PQC readiness. Partner on strategy, roadmap decisions, and customer discussions across Azure Key Vault, Managed HSM, external key management, key-protection libraries, and HSM platforms.


Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree AND 8+ years experience in product/service/program management or software development
    • OR equivalent experience.
 
Other Requirements:
Candidates must be able to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:
  • Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Significant product-management experience in security, cloud infrastructure, cryptography, key management, identity, or compliance.
  • Proven ability to define KPIs and drive measurable results across teams you do not directly manage.
  • Customer-facing experience presenting technical roadmaps and translating customer, regulatory, and government requirements into product decisions.
  • Strong product judgment translating standards, compliance obligations, and technical dependencies into priorities, sequencing, and tradeoffs.
  • Clear executive communication and demonstrated influence across engineering, field, compliance, legal, policy, and governance teams.
  • Familiarity with post-quantum cryptography, including ML-KEM, ML-DSA, hybrid transition patterns, or CNSA 2.0; cloud key management and HSMs; large-scale cryptographic migrations; and security governance or compliance programs.

Overview

Microsoft's transition to quantum-safe cryptography is a company-wide, multi-year change spanning encryption in transit, Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), and encryption at rest. Success requires more than publishing standards or building foundational components. Microsoft needs a reliable way to measure adoption, expose gaps, assign accountability, and drive decisions across organizations that own their own roadmaps. Key Management is a critical product area in the transition. Quantum-safe outcomes depend on the readiness of key-management services, key hierarchies, Hardware Security Modules (HSM) hardware and firmware, and related compliance dependencies.

As a Principal Product Manager for Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) Adoption & Key Management, you will define what readiness means, what Microsoft measures, and how leaders act on the evidence. You will work closely with the Key Management team on its PQC product strategy and roadmap, while using that product work as a proving ground for the broader adoption model. Your job is to make the transition concrete: clear requirements, measurable progress, explicit owners, sequenced dependencies, and credible commitments to leadership, customers, and regulators.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
 
 
In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day.


Responsibilities
  • Define PQC readiness and measurement. Own outcome targets, KPIs, scorecards, telemetry requirements, and adoption bars across encryption in transit, PKI, and encryption at rest.
  • Drive accountable cross-team results. Use existing governance and reviews to turn gaps or missed targets into named blockers, owners, decisions, and checkpoints.
  • Lead customer, field, compliance, and CELA engagement. Present Microsoft's PQC direction and translate customer, audit, regulatory, and government requirements into product priorities and timelines.
  • Own the product roadmap and adoption narrative. Publish clear PQC roadmaps and guidance that distinguish committed capabilities from plans, dependencies, exceptions, and open decisions.
  • Support Key Management PQC readiness. Partner on strategy, roadmap decisions, and customer discussions across Azure Key Vault, Managed HSM, external key management, key-protection libraries, and HSM platforms.


Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree AND 8+ years experience in product/service/program management or software development
    • OR equivalent experience.
 
Other Requirements:
Candidates must be able to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:
  • Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Significant product-management experience in security, cloud infrastructure, cryptography, key management, identity, or compliance.
  • Proven ability to define KPIs and drive measurable results across teams you do not directly manage.
  • Customer-facing experience presenting technical roadmaps and translating customer, regulatory, and government requirements into product decisions.
  • Strong product judgment translating standards, compliance obligations, and technical dependencies into priorities, sequencing, and tradeoffs.
  • Clear executive communication and demonstrated influence across engineering, field, compliance, legal, policy, and governance teams.
  • Familiarity with post-quantum cryptography, including ML-KEM, ML-DSA, hybrid transition patterns, or CNSA 2.0; cloud key management and HSMs; large-scale cryptographic migrations; and security governance or compliance programs.

About the job

When leading companies choose Google Cloud, it's a huge win for spreading the power of cloud computing globally. Once educational institutions, government agencies, and other businesses sign on to use Google Cloud products, you come in to facilitate making their work more productive, mobile, and collaborative. You listen and deliver what is most helpful for the customer. You assist fellow sales Googlers by problem-solving key technical issues for our customers. You liaise with the product marketing management and engineering teams to stay on top of industry trends and devise enhancements to Google Cloud products.

As a Customer Engineer, you will help grow our cyber security business by building and expanding relationships with new and existing customers. You will be a trusted advisor to customers and an advocate for our security solutions. You will provide support to C-level, security leaders, cloud security architects and security analysts, using both technical and business skill sets to lead projects forward. You will accompany customers in discovering the technology/solution and consult around the best way to secure and ensure compliance. You will optimize for results when in production, leading with empathy, while identifying innovative ways to multiply the impact of the team.

Google Cloud accelerates every organization’s ability to digitally transform its business and industry. We deliver enterprise-grade solutions that leverage Google’s technology, and tools that help developers build more sustainably. Customers in more than 200 countries and territories turn to Google Cloud as their trusted partner to enable growth and solve their most critical business problems.

Responsibilities

  • Work with the team to identify and qualify business opportunities, understand customer technical objections, and develop the strategy to resolve technical blockers.
  • Work directly with customers to demonstrate and prototype Google Cloud product integrations in customer/partner environments.
  • Recommend integration strategies, enterprise architectures, platforms, and application infrastructure required to complete solutions using best practices on Google Cloud.

Across the node data plane, you will lead deep systems security architecture across hypervisors, virtual machine monitors (VMMs), host operating systems, kernel subsystems, and hardware-level isolation mechanisms.

Overview

Global Workplace Services (GWS) plans, delivers, and operates Microsoft's global real estate portfolio of approximately 40 million square feet (SF) across an outsourced, multi-region delivery model. This role provides the global operating backbone for Transaction Management and portfolio planning by establishing consistent frameworks, governance, analytics, and decision tools that improve visibility, strengthen controls, and enable more timely, data-informed real estate decisions.

As that portfolio grows more dynamic, GWS needs consistent, well-governed frameworks for how transactions are planned and executed and how portfolio strategy is shaped by data.

The Senior Program Manager will be responsible for creating the methodologies supporting portfolio scenario planning, demand planning, and transaction analytics. The role will translate regional and business requirements into scalable standards, tools, and operating practices. Regional leadership and the GWS leadership team retain accountability for regional and global portfolio strategy and transaction decisions.



Responsibilities

 

Transaction Management Frameworks & Process

  • Define, document, and continuously improve the Transaction Management operating model (playbooks, process flows, templates, and RACI) across the full deal lifecycle of leasing, renewals, acquisitions, and dispositions and the outsourced Tier 1 model.
  • Establish minimum global standards for transaction initiation, evaluation, approval, documentation, execution and closeout, driving global consistency, while enabling appropriate regional and market flexibility.
  • Lead the global Transaction Management rhythm of business, including pipeline governance, portfolio reviews, escalation management, scorecards, and performance reporting with TM Regional Leads and Tier 1 partners.
  • Drive adoption and compliance with global Transaction Management standards, playbooks, tools, and processes, using performance insights, stakeholder feedback and lessons learned to continuously improve the operating model and standardize best practices across regions.
  • Partner with TM Regional leads and Tier 1 partners to identify opportunities for improvement and strengthen transaction speed, quality, transparency, and control.

Portfolio Strategy Planning, Scenario Modelling & Decision Support

  • Define the frameworks and methodology for portfolio scenario planning and demand planning, translating business and market signals (headcount, growth, consolidation, and hybrid work) into consistent planning assumptions and real estate requirements over a multi-year horizon.
  • Build repeatable models, decision criteria, and planning guidance that enable Portfolio Managers and GWS leadership to evaluate alternatives, understand trade-offs and sequence portfolio actions
  • Integrate cost benchmarking into portfolio planning, deal strategy, and capital decisions, partnering with Capital Planning and Real Estate & Facilities Finance (REFFIN) on align financial assumptions, NPV analysis, and funding implications.
  • Establish a consolidated portfolio-level view of demand, opportunity, risk and transaction pipeline that connects regional planning into one consistent framework.
  • Provide portfolio-level insights and recommendations while preserving regional accountability for strategy development, market decisions, and execution.

Portfolio & Transaction Data Analytics

  • Define the requirements for, and shape the development of, a global real estate strategy tool and dashboard that consolidates lease and market data into portfolio-level intelligence.
  • Establish metric definitions, analytics standards, and data governance for transaction and portfolio data, setting the specifications that support analysts and the Data Platform produce against.
  • Translate analytics into decision-ready recommendations, and pilot AI-assisted capabilities such as demand forecasting, scenario analysis, and reporting automation.

Governance, Operating Model & Continuous Improvement

  • Establish Controls and exception management processes that identify transaction, financial, data-quality, compliance, and delivery risks and ensure timely escalation and resolution.
  • Define authoritative sources, data ownership, and reconciliation requirements for core portfolio and transaction information.
  • Ensure processes, tools, and supplier practices remain aligned with applicable corporate approval, records-management, privacy, legal, and financial-control requirements.
  • Define the TM specific service requirements, deliverables, performance measures, and governance framework within the Tier 1 operating model, ensuring alignment with corporate transaction policies, capital approval requirements, and enterprise controls.
  • Partner on the outsourced (Tier 1) operating model (scope, SOW alignment, scorecards, and RACI) and keep frameworks aligned with corporate transaction and capital-approval policy.
  • Define and report program success measures such as cycle-time, data-accuracy, and adoption metrics.
  • Lead discovery and value-stream reviews to remove friction and waste and bring corporate real estate best practices and innovation into GWS.

Stakeholder Partnership & Influence

  • Partner across GWS regions, Capital Planning, Finance, GWS Technology, the Data Platform, and CELA, together with Tier 1 partners, and influence outcomes without direct authority.
  • Represent the transaction and portfolio-strategy platform in business reviews and leadership forums.


Qualifications

Required / Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in business management, Real Estate, Finance, Project Management, Data or Business Analytics, or related field AND 6+ years of experience in real estate portfolio management, transaction management, real estate strategy or planning, or related work, OR 8+ years of equivalent experience.

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Demonstrated experience defining or improving processes, playbooks, or operating models in a real estate, facilities, or comparable enterprise-operations context.
  • Experience translating data and analysis into frameworks, standards, or decisions for senior stakeholders.
  • Bachelor's Degree in a related field AND 8+ years of relevant experience, including direct experience in real estate transaction management and portfolio strategy or planning.
  • Experience with corporate real estate transactions across multiple regions and an outsourced service-delivery (Tier 1) model.
  • Experience designing scenario- and demand-planning frameworks and connecting them to space and capital decisions.
  • Proficiency interpreting business intelligence and portfolio data (for example, Power BI) and setting metric and analytics standards; familiarity with lease and market data and real estate financial analysis such as lease-versus-buy and NPV.
  • Professional credentials such as MCR (CoreNet Global) or an MBA; experience applying AI-assisted tools to forecasting, scenario analysis, or reporting automation.

Commercial Real Estate Analysis

Transaction Management

Financial Analysis

Forecasting

Portfolio & Demand Planning

Process Design & Operational Excellence

Governance Methodology & Practices

Program Management

Data Visualization & Business Intelligence

Business Technology Optimization

Change Management

Overview

Global Workplace Services (GWS) plans, delivers, and operates Microsoft's global real estate portfolio of approximately 40 million square feet (SF) across an outsourced, multi-region delivery model. This role provides the global operating backbone for Transaction Management and portfolio planning by establishing consistent frameworks, governance, analytics, and decision tools that improve visibility, strengthen controls, and enable more timely, data-informed real estate decisions.

As that portfolio grows more dynamic, GWS needs consistent, well-governed frameworks for how transactions are planned and executed and how portfolio strategy is shaped by data.

The Senior Program Manager will be responsible for creating the methodologies supporting portfolio scenario planning, demand planning, and transaction analytics. The role will translate regional and business requirements into scalable standards, tools, and operating practices. Regional leadership and the GWS leadership team retain accountability for regional and global portfolio strategy and transaction decisions.



Responsibilities

 

Transaction Management Frameworks & Process

  • Define, document, and continuously improve the Transaction Management operating model (playbooks, process flows, templates, and RACI) across the full deal lifecycle of leasing, renewals, acquisitions, and dispositions and the outsourced Tier 1 model.
  • Establish minimum global standards for transaction initiation, evaluation, approval, documentation, execution and closeout, driving global consistency, while enabling appropriate regional and market flexibility.
  • Lead the global Transaction Management rhythm of business, including pipeline governance, portfolio reviews, escalation management, scorecards, and performance reporting with TM Regional Leads and Tier 1 partners.
  • Drive adoption and compliance with global Transaction Management standards, playbooks, tools, and processes, using performance insights, stakeholder feedback and lessons learned to continuously improve the operating model and standardize best practices across regions.
  • Partner with TM Regional leads and Tier 1 partners to identify opportunities for improvement and strengthen transaction speed, quality, transparency, and control.

Portfolio Strategy Planning, Scenario Modelling & Decision Support

  • Define the frameworks and methodology for portfolio scenario planning and demand planning, translating business and market signals (headcount, growth, consolidation, and hybrid work) into consistent planning assumptions and real estate requirements over a multi-year horizon.
  • Build repeatable models, decision criteria, and planning guidance that enable Portfolio Managers and GWS leadership to evaluate alternatives, understand trade-offs and sequence portfolio actions
  • Integrate cost benchmarking into portfolio planning, deal strategy, and capital decisions, partnering with Capital Planning and Real Estate & Facilities Finance (REFFIN) on align financial assumptions, NPV analysis, and funding implications.
  • Establish a consolidated portfolio-level view of demand, opportunity, risk and transaction pipeline that connects regional planning into one consistent framework.
  • Provide portfolio-level insights and recommendations while preserving regional accountability for strategy development, market decisions, and execution.

Portfolio & Transaction Data Analytics

  • Define the requirements for, and shape the development of, a global real estate strategy tool and dashboard that consolidates lease and market data into portfolio-level intelligence.
  • Establish metric definitions, analytics standards, and data governance for transaction and portfolio data, setting the specifications that support analysts and the Data Platform produce against.
  • Translate analytics into decision-ready recommendations, and pilot AI-assisted capabilities such as demand forecasting, scenario analysis, and reporting automation.

Governance, Operating Model & Continuous Improvement

  • Establish Controls and exception management processes that identify transaction, financial, data-quality, compliance, and delivery risks and ensure timely escalation and resolution.
  • Define authoritative sources, data ownership, and reconciliation requirements for core portfolio and transaction information.
  • Ensure processes, tools, and supplier practices remain aligned with applicable corporate approval, records-management, privacy, legal, and financial-control requirements.
  • Define the TM specific service requirements, deliverables, performance measures, and governance framework within the Tier 1 operating model, ensuring alignment with corporate transaction policies, capital approval requirements, and enterprise controls.
  • Partner on the outsourced (Tier 1) operating model (scope, SOW alignment, scorecards, and RACI) and keep frameworks aligned with corporate transaction and capital-approval policy.
  • Define and report program success measures such as cycle-time, data-accuracy, and adoption metrics.
  • Lead discovery and value-stream reviews to remove friction and waste and bring corporate real estate best practices and innovation into GWS.

Stakeholder Partnership & Influence

  • Partner across GWS regions, Capital Planning, Finance, GWS Technology, the Data Platform, and CELA, together with Tier 1 partners, and influence outcomes without direct authority.
  • Represent the transaction and portfolio-strategy platform in business reviews and leadership forums.


Qualifications

Required / Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in business management, Real Estate, Finance, Project Management, Data or Business Analytics, or related field AND 6+ years of experience in real estate portfolio management, transaction management, real estate strategy or planning, or related work, OR 8+ years of equivalent experience.

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Demonstrated experience defining or improving processes, playbooks, or operating models in a real estate, facilities, or comparable enterprise-operations context.
  • Experience translating data and analysis into frameworks, standards, or decisions for senior stakeholders.
  • Bachelor's Degree in a related field AND 8+ years of relevant experience, including direct experience in real estate transaction management and portfolio strategy or planning.
  • Experience with corporate real estate transactions across multiple regions and an outsourced service-delivery (Tier 1) model.
  • Experience designing scenario- and demand-planning frameworks and connecting them to space and capital decisions.
  • Proficiency interpreting business intelligence and portfolio data (for example, Power BI) and setting metric and analytics standards; familiarity with lease and market data and real estate financial analysis such as lease-versus-buy and NPV.
  • Professional credentials such as MCR (CoreNet Global) or an MBA; experience applying AI-assisted tools to forecasting, scenario analysis, or reporting automation.

Skills

Core skills for this role, drawn from the Real Estate Portfolio Management IC4 career-stage profile and calibrated to a frameworks, transaction-management, and analytics remit:

Commercial Real Estate Analysis

Transaction Management

Financial Analysis

Forecasting

Portfolio & Demand Planning

Process Design & Operational Excellence

Governance Methodology & Practices

Program Management

Data Visualization & Business Intelligence

Business Technology Optimization

Change Management

Stakeholder Management

Decision Making

Written & Oral Communication

Overview

Global Workplace Services (GWS) plans, delivers, and operates Microsoft's global real estate portfolio of approximately 40 million square feet (SF) across an outsourced, multi-region delivery model. This role provides the global operating backbone for Transaction Management and portfolio planning by establishing consistent frameworks, governance, analytics, and decision tools that improve visibility, strengthen controls, and enable more timely, data-informed real estate decisions.

As that portfolio grows more dynamic, GWS needs consistent, well-governed frameworks for how transactions are planned and executed and how portfolio strategy is shaped by data.

The Senior Program Manager will be responsible for creating the methodologies supporting portfolio scenario planning, demand planning, and transaction analytics. The role will translate regional and business requirements into scalable standards, tools, and operating practices. Regional leadership and the GWS leadership team retain accountability for regional and global portfolio strategy and transaction decisions.



Responsibilities

 

Transaction Management Frameworks & Process

  • Define, document, and continuously improve the Transaction Management operating model (playbooks, process flows, templates, and RACI) across the full deal lifecycle of leasing, renewals, acquisitions, and dispositions and the outsourced Tier 1 model.
  • Establish minimum global standards for transaction initiation, evaluation, approval, documentation, execution and closeout, driving global consistency, while enabling appropriate regional and market flexibility.
  • Lead the global Transaction Management rhythm of business, including pipeline governance, portfolio reviews, escalation management, scorecards, and performance reporting with TM Regional Leads and Tier 1 partners.
  • Drive adoption and compliance with global Transaction Management standards, playbooks, tools, and processes, using performance insights, stakeholder feedback and lessons learned to continuously improve the operating model and standardize best practices across regions.
  • Partner with TM Regional leads and Tier 1 partners to identify opportunities for improvement and strengthen transaction speed, quality, transparency, and control.

Portfolio Strategy Planning, Scenario Modelling & Decision Support

  • Define the frameworks and methodology for portfolio scenario planning and demand planning, translating business and market signals (headcount, growth, consolidation, and hybrid work) into consistent planning assumptions and real estate requirements over a multi-year horizon.
  • Build repeatable models, decision criteria, and planning guidance that enable Portfolio Managers and GWS leadership to evaluate alternatives, understand trade-offs and sequence portfolio actions
  • Integrate cost benchmarking into portfolio planning, deal strategy, and capital decisions, partnering with Capital Planning and Real Estate & Facilities Finance (REFFIN) on align financial assumptions, NPV analysis, and funding implications.
  • Establish a consolidated portfolio-level view of demand, opportunity, risk and transaction pipeline that connects regional planning into one consistent framework.
  • Provide portfolio-level insights and recommendations while preserving regional accountability for strategy development, market decisions, and execution.

Portfolio & Transaction Data Analytics

  • Define the requirements for, and shape the development of, a global real estate strategy tool and dashboard that consolidates lease and market data into portfolio-level intelligence.
  • Establish metric definitions, analytics standards, and data governance for transaction and portfolio data, setting the specifications that support analysts and the Data Platform produce against.
  • Translate analytics into decision-ready recommendations, and pilot AI-assisted capabilities such as demand forecasting, scenario analysis, and reporting automation.

Governance, Operating Model & Continuous Improvement

  • Establish Controls and exception management processes that identify transaction, financial, data-quality, compliance, and delivery risks and ensure timely escalation and resolution.
  • Define authoritative sources, data ownership, and reconciliation requirements for core portfolio and transaction information.
  • Ensure processes, tools, and supplier practices remain aligned with applicable corporate approval, records-management, privacy, legal, and financial-control requirements.
  • Define the TM specific service requirements, deliverables, performance measures, and governance framework within the Tier 1 operating model, ensuring alignment with corporate transaction policies, capital approval requirements, and enterprise controls.
  • Partner on the outsourced (Tier 1) operating model (scope, SOW alignment, scorecards, and RACI) and keep frameworks aligned with corporate transaction and capital-approval policy.
  • Define and report program success measures such as cycle-time, data-accuracy, and adoption metrics.
  • Lead discovery and value-stream reviews to remove friction and waste and bring corporate real estate best practices and innovation into GWS.

Stakeholder Partnership & Influence

  • Partner across GWS regions, Capital Planning, Finance, GWS Technology, the Data Platform, and CELA, together with Tier 1 partners, and influence outcomes without direct authority.
  • Represent the transaction and portfolio-strategy platform in business reviews and leadership forums.


Qualifications

Required / Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in business management, Real Estate, Finance, Project Management, Data or Business Analytics, or related field AND 6+ years of experience in real estate portfolio management, transaction management, real estate strategy or planning, or related work, OR 8+ years of equivalent experience.

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Demonstrated experience defining or improving processes, playbooks, or operating models in a real estate, facilities, or comparable enterprise-operations context.
  • Experience translating data and analysis into frameworks, standards, or decisions for senior stakeholders.
  • Bachelor's Degree in a related field AND 8+ years of relevant experience, including direct experience in real estate transaction management and portfolio strategy or planning.
  • Experience with corporate real estate transactions across multiple regions and an outsourced service-delivery (Tier 1) model.
  • Experience designing scenario- and demand-planning frameworks and connecting them to space and capital decisions.
  • Proficiency interpreting business intelligence and portfolio data (for example, Power BI) and setting metric and analytics standards; familiarity with lease and market data and real estate financial analysis such as lease-versus-buy and NPV.
  • Professional credentials such as MCR (CoreNet Global) or an MBA; experience applying AI-assisted tools to forecasting, scenario analysis, or reporting automation.

Portfolio & Demand Planning

Program Management

Business Technology Optimization

Change Management

Overview

Global Workplace Services (GWS) plans, delivers, and operates Microsoft's global real estate portfolio of approximately 40 million square feet (SF) across an outsourced, multi-region delivery model. This role provides the global operating backbone for Transaction Management and portfolio planning by establishing consistent frameworks, governance, analytics, and decision tools that improve visibility, strengthen controls, and enable more timely, data-informed real estate decisions.

As that portfolio grows more dynamic, GWS needs consistent, well-governed frameworks for how transactions are planned and executed and how portfolio strategy is shaped by data.

The Senior Program Manager will be responsible for creating the methodologies supporting portfolio scenario planning, demand planning, and transaction analytics. The role will translate regional and business requirements into scalable standards, tools, and operating practices. Regional leadership and the GWS leadership team retain accountability for regional and global portfolio strategy and transaction decisions.



Responsibilities

 

Transaction Management Frameworks & Process

  • Define, document, and continuously improve the Transaction Management operating model (playbooks, process flows, templates, and RACI) across the full deal lifecycle of leasing, renewals, acquisitions, and dispositions and the outsourced Tier 1 model.
  • Establish minimum global standards for transaction initiation, evaluation, approval, documentation, execution and closeout, driving global consistency, while enabling appropriate regional and market flexibility.
  • Lead the global Transaction Management rhythm of business, including pipeline governance, portfolio reviews, escalation management, scorecards, and performance reporting with TM Regional Leads and Tier 1 partners.
  • Drive adoption and compliance with global Transaction Management standards, playbooks, tools, and processes, using performance insights, stakeholder feedback and lessons learned to continuously improve the operating model and standardize best practices across regions.
  • Partner with TM Regional leads and Tier 1 partners to identify opportunities for improvement and strengthen transaction speed, quality, transparency, and control.

Portfolio Strategy Planning, Scenario Modelling & Decision Support

  • Define the frameworks and methodology for portfolio scenario planning and demand planning, translating business and market signals (headcount, growth, consolidation, and hybrid work) into consistent planning assumptions and real estate requirements over a multi-year horizon.
  • Build repeatable models, decision criteria, and planning guidance that enable Portfolio Managers and GWS leadership to evaluate alternatives, understand trade-offs and sequence portfolio actions
  • Integrate cost benchmarking into portfolio planning, deal strategy, and capital decisions, partnering with Capital Planning and Real Estate & Facilities Finance (REFFIN) on align financial assumptions, NPV analysis, and funding implications.
  • Establish a consolidated portfolio-level view of demand, opportunity, risk and transaction pipeline that connects regional planning into one consistent framework.
  • Provide portfolio-level insights and recommendations while preserving regional accountability for strategy development, market decisions, and execution.

Portfolio & Transaction Data Analytics

  • Define the requirements for, and shape the development of, a global real estate strategy tool and dashboard that consolidates lease and market data into portfolio-level intelligence.
  • Establish metric definitions, analytics standards, and data governance for transaction and portfolio data, setting the specifications that support analysts and the Data Platform produce against.
  • Translate analytics into decision-ready recommendations, and pilot AI-assisted capabilities such as demand forecasting, scenario analysis, and reporting automation.

Governance, Operating Model & Continuous Improvement

  • Establish Controls and exception management processes that identify transaction, financial, data-quality, compliance, and delivery risks and ensure timely escalation and resolution.
  • Define authoritative sources, data ownership, and reconciliation requirements for core portfolio and transaction information.
  • Ensure processes, tools, and supplier practices remain aligned with applicable corporate approval, records-management, privacy, legal, and financial-control requirements.
  • Define the TM specific service requirements, deliverables, performance measures, and governance framework within the Tier 1 operating model, ensuring alignment with corporate transaction policies, capital approval requirements, and enterprise controls.
  • Partner on the outsourced (Tier 1) operating model (scope, SOW alignment, scorecards, and RACI) and keep frameworks aligned with corporate transaction and capital-approval policy.
  • Define and report program success measures such as cycle-time, data-accuracy, and adoption metrics.
  • Lead discovery and value-stream reviews to remove friction and waste and bring corporate real estate best practices and innovation into GWS.

Stakeholder Partnership & Influence

  • Partner across GWS regions, Capital Planning, Finance, GWS Technology, the Data Platform, and CELA, together with Tier 1 partners, and influence outcomes without direct authority.
  • Represent the transaction and portfolio-strategy platform in business reviews and leadership forums.


Qualifications

Required / Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in business management, Real Estate, Finance, Project Management, Data or Business Analytics, or related field AND 6+ years of experience in real estate portfolio management, transaction management, real estate strategy or planning, or related work, OR 8+ years of equivalent experience.

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Demonstrated experience defining or improving processes, playbooks, or operating models in a real estate, facilities, or comparable enterprise-operations context.
  • Experience translating data and analysis into frameworks, standards, or decisions for senior stakeholders.
  • Bachelor's Degree in a related field AND 8+ years of relevant experience, including direct experience in real estate transaction management and portfolio strategy or planning.
  • Experience with corporate real estate transactions across multiple regions and an outsourced service-delivery (Tier 1) model.
  • Experience designing scenario- and demand-planning frameworks and connecting them to space and capital decisions.
  • Proficiency interpreting business intelligence and portfolio data (for example, Power BI) and setting metric and analytics standards; familiarity with lease and market data and real estate financial analysis such as lease-versus-buy and NPV.
  • Professional credentials such as MCR (CoreNet Global) or an MBA; experience applying AI-assisted tools to forecasting, scenario analysis, or reporting automation.

Skills

Core skills for this role, drawn from the Real Estate Portfolio Management IC4 career-stage profile and calibrated to a frameworks, transaction-management, and analytics remit:

Commercial Real Estate Analysis

Transaction Management

Financial Analysis

Forecasting

Portfolio & Demand Planning

Process Design & Operational Excellence

Governance Methodology & Practices

Program Management

Data Visualization & Business Intelligence

Business Technology Optimization

Change Management

Stakeholder Management

Decision Making

Written & Oral Communication

Overview

Global Workplace Services (GWS) plans, delivers, and operates Microsoft's global real estate portfolio of approximately 40 million square feet (SF) across an outsourced, multi-region delivery model. This role provides the global operating backbone for Transaction Management and portfolio planning by establishing consistent frameworks, governance, analytics, and decision tools that improve visibility, strengthen controls, and enable more timely, data-informed real estate decisions.

As that portfolio grows more dynamic, GWS needs consistent, well-governed frameworks for how transactions are planned and executed and how portfolio strategy is shaped by data.

The Senior Program Manager will be responsible for creating the methodologies supporting portfolio scenario planning, demand planning, and transaction analytics. The role will translate regional and business requirements into scalable standards, tools, and operating practices. Regional leadership and the GWS leadership team retain accountability for regional and global portfolio strategy and transaction decisions.



Responsibilities

 

Transaction Management Frameworks & Process

  • Define, document, and continuously improve the Transaction Management operating model (playbooks, process flows, templates, and RACI) across the full deal lifecycle of leasing, renewals, acquisitions, and dispositions and the outsourced Tier 1 model.
  • Establish minimum global standards for transaction initiation, evaluation, approval, documentation, execution and closeout, driving global consistency, while enabling appropriate regional and market flexibility.
  • Lead the global Transaction Management rhythm of business, including pipeline governance, portfolio reviews, escalation management, scorecards, and performance reporting with TM Regional Leads and Tier 1 partners.
  • Drive adoption and compliance with global Transaction Management standards, playbooks, tools, and processes, using performance insights, stakeholder feedback and lessons learned to continuously improve the operating model and standardize best practices across regions.
  • Partner with TM Regional leads and Tier 1 partners to identify opportunities for improvement and strengthen transaction speed, quality, transparency, and control.

Portfolio Strategy Planning, Scenario Modelling & Decision Support

  • Define the frameworks and methodology for portfolio scenario planning and demand planning, translating business and market signals (headcount, growth, consolidation, and hybrid work) into consistent planning assumptions and real estate requirements over a multi-year horizon.
  • Build repeatable models, decision criteria, and planning guidance that enable Portfolio Managers and GWS leadership to evaluate alternatives, understand trade-offs and sequence portfolio actions
  • Integrate cost benchmarking into portfolio planning, deal strategy, and capital decisions, partnering with Capital Planning and Real Estate & Facilities Finance (REFFIN) on align financial assumptions, NPV analysis, and funding implications.
  • Establish a consolidated portfolio-level view of demand, opportunity, risk and transaction pipeline that connects regional planning into one consistent framework.
  • Provide portfolio-level insights and recommendations while preserving regional accountability for strategy development, market decisions, and execution.

Portfolio & Transaction Data Analytics

  • Define the requirements for, and shape the development of, a global real estate strategy tool and dashboard that consolidates lease and market data into portfolio-level intelligence.
  • Establish metric definitions, analytics standards, and data governance for transaction and portfolio data, setting the specifications that support analysts and the Data Platform produce against.
  • Translate analytics into decision-ready recommendations, and pilot AI-assisted capabilities such as demand forecasting, scenario analysis, and reporting automation.

Governance, Operating Model & Continuous Improvement

  • Establish Controls and exception management processes that identify transaction, financial, data-quality, compliance, and delivery risks and ensure timely escalation and resolution.
  • Define authoritative sources, data ownership, and reconciliation requirements for core portfolio and transaction information.
  • Ensure processes, tools, and supplier practices remain aligned with applicable corporate approval, records-management, privacy, legal, and financial-control requirements.
  • Define the TM specific service requirements, deliverables, performance measures, and governance framework within the Tier 1 operating model, ensuring alignment with corporate transaction policies, capital approval requirements, and enterprise controls.
  • Partner on the outsourced (Tier 1) operating model (scope, SOW alignment, scorecards, and RACI) and keep frameworks aligned with corporate transaction and capital-approval policy.
  • Define and report program success measures such as cycle-time, data-accuracy, and adoption metrics.
  • Lead discovery and value-stream reviews to remove friction and waste and bring corporate real estate best practices and innovation into GWS.

Stakeholder Partnership & Influence

  • Partner across GWS regions, Capital Planning, Finance, GWS Technology, the Data Platform, and CELA, together with Tier 1 partners, and influence outcomes without direct authority.
  • Represent the transaction and portfolio-strategy platform in business reviews and leadership forums.


Qualifications

Required / Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in business management, Real Estate, Finance, Project Management, Data or Business Analytics, or related field AND 6+ years of experience in real estate portfolio management, transaction management, real estate strategy or planning, or related work, OR 8+ years of equivalent experience.

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Demonstrated experience defining or improving processes, playbooks, or operating models in a real estate, facilities, or comparable enterprise-operations context.
  • Experience translating data and analysis into frameworks, standards, or decisions for senior stakeholders.
  • Bachelor's Degree in a related field AND 8+ years of relevant experience, including direct experience in real estate transaction management and portfolio strategy or planning.
  • Experience with corporate real estate transactions across multiple regions and an outsourced service-delivery (Tier 1) model.
  • Experience designing scenario- and demand-planning frameworks and connecting them to space and capital decisions.
  • Proficiency interpreting business intelligence and portfolio data (for example, Power BI) and setting metric and analytics standards; familiarity with lease and market data and real estate financial analysis such as lease-versus-buy and NPV.
  • Professional credentials such as MCR (CoreNet Global) or an MBA; experience applying AI-assisted tools to forecasting, scenario analysis, or reporting automation.

Portfolio & Demand Planning

Process Design & Operational Excellence

Governance Methodology & Practices

Program Management

Data Visualization & Business Intelligence

Business Technology Optimization

Change Management

Stakeholder Management

Decision Making

Written & Oral Communication

About the job

Like Google's own ambitions, the work of a Software Engineer goes beyond just Search. Software Engineering Managers have not only the technical expertise to take on and provide technical leadership to major projects, but also manage a team of Engineers. You not only optimize your own code but make sure Engineers are able to optimize theirs. As a Software Engineering Manager you manage your project goals, contribute to product strategy and help develop your team. Teams work all across the company, in areas such as information retrieval, artificial intelligence, natural language processing, distributed computing, large-scale system design, networking, security, data compression, user interface design; the list goes on and is growing every day. Operating with scale and speed, our exceptional software engineers are just getting started -- and as a manager, you guide the way.

With technical and leadership expertise, you manage engineers across multiple teams and locations, a large product budget and oversee the deployment of large-scale projects across multiple sites internationally.

The Privacy, Safety, and Security (PSS) team builds foundational technologies, infrastructure, and frameworks that protect billions of users, safeguard data, and defend global digital ecosystems. As a central engineering and governance pillar, PSS partners across product areas to engineer security-by-design solutions, automate threat detection, advance cryptographic and privacy-preserving architectures, and ensure compliance with global regulatory standards.

In this role, you will be a leader who loves building alongside their team, turning ambitious ideas into working prototypes while coaching and growing the next generation of technical leaders.

The Core team builds the technical foundation behind Google’s flagship products. We are owners and advocates for the underlying design elements, developer platforms, product components, and infrastructure at Google. We look across Google’s products to build central solutions, break down technical barriers and strengthen existing systems. As the Core team, we have a mandate and a unique opportunity to impact important technical decisions across the company.

About the job

Google's software engineers develop the next-generation technologies that change how billions of users connect, explore, and interact with information and one another. Our products need to handle information at massive scale, and extend well beyond web search. We're looking for engineers who bring fresh ideas from all areas, including information retrieval, distributed computing, large-scale system design, networking and data storage, security, artificial intelligence, natural language processing, UI design and mobile; the list goes on and is growing every day. As a software engineer, you will work on a specific project critical to Google’s needs with opportunities to switch teams and projects as you and our fast-paced business grow and evolve. We need our engineers to be versatile, display leadership qualities and be enthusiastic to take on new problems across the full-stack as we continue to push technology forward.

With your technical expertise you will manage project priorities, deadlines, and deliverables. You will design, develop, test, deploy, maintain, and enhance software solutions.

Defend the security firmware and hardware foundation of the world’s most critical infrastructure.
